title: The Alms Road
text: The granary echoes when you knock on it. {monk} offers to take the alms road down to the Shannon farms, as the old brothers did, and beg for the house.

choices.label: Send {monk} with a bag and a blessing
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} went down the alms road to the Shannon farms.

choices.label: Keep every pair of hands at home

title: Lights in the Pylon Field
text: Shepherds speak of lights moving at night among the dead turbines east of {place}. {monk} asks leave to go and see what the old world left behind.

choices.label: Let {monk} go and search
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} went east to search the turbine field.

choices.label: Leave the dead city to the dead

title: A Boy at the Gate
text: A boy from the glen village has run through the night. His grandmother is dying and asks for a man of the old faith to pray with her. {monk} could reach the village in two days.

choices.label: Send {monk} at once
choices.chronicle: {When}, a boy came running from the glen village, and {monk} went back with him to a deathbed.

choices.label: No one can be spared
choices.chronicle: {When}, the glen village asked for a brother to pray at a deathbed, and the house sent no one. The village did not forget it.

title: The Drowned Church
text: {monk} asks leave to walk to the drowned church at Inishkeel, where the sea took the old cathedral and the bells are said to ring under the water at low tide. It is six weeks there and back.

choices.label: Give him leave and your blessing
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} set out on pilgrimage to the drowned church at Inishkeel.

yes.chronicle: {monk} came home with a cart of grain from the Shannon farms, and their blessings with it.

no.chronicle: {monk} came home with almost nothing, and with word that riders of the Tollmaster were taking tolls on the Shannon road.

effects.chronicle: {monk} was stopped on the Shannon road by the Tollmaster's riders. They took the grain, beat him for having so little, and let him walk home.

title: Something from the Old World
text: {monk} returns from the turbine field with a box of grey metal, warm to the touch. Inside it, something hums.

choices.label: Keep it in the workshop and study it
choices.chronicle: {monk} brought back from the turbine field a humming box of the old world, and it was kept in the workshop.

choices.label: Bury it where no one will find it
choices.chronicle: {monk} brought back a humming box from the turbine field. {abbot} had it buried outside the walls, in ground that was never blessed.

effects.chronicle: {monk} came back from the ruins with two books of the old world, swollen with damp but still legible.
{monk} came back from the turbine field bleeding, and for a long time would not say what he had met there.

yes.chronicle: {monk} came back from the glen village. The old woman had died at peace, and the village said they would remember who came.

no.chronicle: {monk} reached the glen village too late, and could only help bury the dead. He came home quiet.

effects.chronicle: {monk} came home from Inishkeel, thinner and full of joy, and said he had heard them ring.

The weeks passed and {monk} did not come home from Inishkeel. A trader brought word that a monk had died of fever at the shrine and was buried there, within sound of the bells. The brothers said the Office of the Dead for him.

yes.chronicle: {monk} came down from the hermit's cave after a month alone, and sang the Office that night as he had not sung it in years.

no.chronicle: {monk} did not come back from the hermit's cave. He sent word by a shepherd that he had gone to look for God elsewhere, and asked the brothers to pray for him.

yes.chronicle: {monk} spent two weeks mending roofs in the glen village. When he left, the headman walked him to the edge of the fields.

no.chronicle: {monk} went to the glen village to make amends, but they would not open their doors to him.
